page.layout: Two printed pages on the scan. Left page: running head with page number at top left and the chapter heading at top right; one main text column with Hebrew and Greek words; a narrow margin of notes at the left edge; a Hebrew catchword line at the foot. Right page: only a fragment of a column edge is visible, too cut off to transcribe.

main_text.p: sam; & locum illius voraginis. Hic autem pro loco sumit, nè hoc idem sit cum eo quod sequitur, [illegible, ~12 letters]. At ego in hoc nullum video periculum; & ipse fatetur utrumque eodem pene recidere. Arbitror Tebom non nisi duplici isto modo, prout hic notavit Merocerus, usurpari hoc autem in loco pro aquarum voragine accipi, quæ propria est vocis significatio; quemadmodum mare & fluvius primo ac proprie aquas denotant, licèt metonymicè etiam pro loco aquarum, seu alveo usurpentur. Quòd autem hic cum aquis alia erant permixta, id ex accidenti fuit, nec novam aliquam vocis acceptionem arguit.

[illegible, ~6 letters] Et Spiritus Domini.] Sic Vulg. & Septuag. Targ. Hierosolym. * Et spiritus misericordiarum à facie Domini. Ruach autem & ventum significat, atque ita Onkelos hic accepisse videtur, [illegible, ~8 letters] et ventus à conspectu Domini flubat super faciem aquarum. Fagius etiam tellatur plerosque ex Hebræis hic ventum intelligere, qui ob vehementiam, quæ aquarum molem agitavit, eum quòd à Deo in eum finem missus esset, Ventus Dei hic appellatur. Ita quidem Abben Ezra ait vocari Muoh Elohim, ventum Dei, [illegible, ~6 letters], id est, spiritum quòd missus esset voluntate Dei ad exsiccandas aquas. R. Salom interpretatur [illegible, ~6 letters], i.e. spiritus ejus, & verbum sustentationis ejus. Hunc locum ad ventum retulisse multos Græcos & Latinos Expositores testatur Sehensis, Bibl. S. lib. 5, annotat. 7. Eorum autem sententiam sequendam arbitror, qui de Spiritu Sancto intelligendum censent.

page.notes: Left margin notes are very faint and partly illegible; the note beside "Et spiritus" reads "Ex sic Targum Jonathan". The right page is a cut-off fragment of another column and is not transcribed. Several Hebrew words are illegible from the scan and are marked accordingly. The printed page number is 6 and the chapter heading reads "Gap. i." Catchword and signature at the foot are very faint.
